S1::what % of customers r repeat custome.sql:
WITH valid_orders AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_unique_id
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
),
per_customer AS (
  SELECT customer_unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS order_count
  FROM valid_orders
  GROUP BY customer_unique_id
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_count >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS repeat_customer_pct
FROM per_customer;
S1::what % of customers r repeat custome.explanation: Shares of customers (unique customer_unique_id) with 2 or more valid orders out of all customers with at least one valid order, returned as a percentage.
assumptions: Customer = customers.customer_unique_id
Valid order = order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable'), over all time
Percentage requested, so the share is multiplied by 100

S4::what % of customers r repeat custome.sql:

  SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_unique_id

  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id

),
cust_counts AS (
  SELECT customer_unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS n_orders
  FROM valid_orders
  GROUP BY customer_unique_id

S1::number of currently active sellers i.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oi.seller_id) AS active_sellers
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-06-02'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-09-01'
  AND LOWER(p.category_en) IN ('cool_stuff', 'cool stuff');
S1::number of currently active sellers i.explanation: Counts distinct sellers with at least one order item in the cool_stuff category on a valid order purchased between 2018-06-02 and 2018-08-31 inclusive, per the active-seller definition.
assumptions: "Currently active" uses the active-seller rule: at least one order_item on a valid order (status not canceled/unavailable) purchased 2018-06-02 to 2018-08-31 inclusive
Category matched on products.category_en ('cool_stuff', the English name for the cool_stuff category; space/underscore variants accepted)
Filter applied on order_purchase_timestamp

S4::whats the late delivery rate by cust.sql:
SELECT r.region,
       SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(o.order_delivered_customer_date AS DATE) > CAST(o.order_estimated_delivery_date AS DATE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::DOUBLE
         / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS late_rate
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN regions r ON r.state = c.customer_state
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-07-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-08-01'
GROUP BY r.region
ORDER BY late_rate DESC;
S4::whats the late delivery rate by cust.explanation: Late delivery rate (late delivered orders / delivered orders with a delivery date) for orders purchased in July 2018, grouped by the customer's region.
assumptions: "Last month" = July 2018, filtered on order_purchase_timestamp
Late rate = orders with delivered_customer_date > estimated_delivery_date, divided by delivered orders with a non-null delivery date, per the business rules
Region is the customer's region via customers.customer_state joined to regions
Rate returned as a fraction between 0 and 1

S1::which seller state had the worst lat.sql:
WITH os AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    oi.order_id,
    s.seller_state,
    o.order_delivered_customer_date,
    o.order_estimated_delivery_date
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
    AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-01-01'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01'
)
SELECT
  seller_state,
  COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders,
  SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(order_delivered_customer_date AS DATE) > CAST(order_estimated_delivery_date AS DATE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0
    / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS late_rate
FROM os
GROUP BY seller_state
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
ORDER BY late_rate DESC
LIMIT 1;
S1::which seller state had the worst lat.explanation: Computes the 2017 late-delivery rate per seller state (late delivered orders / delivered orders with a delivery date) among states with at least 100 delivered orders, and returns the worst state.
assumptions: 2017 means orders purchased between 2017-01-01 and 2017-12-31 (order_purchase_timestamp, Brazil local time)
Late rate = delivered orders with delivery date after estimated date / delivered orders with a non-null delivery date, per business rules
An order is attributed to every seller state it has items from; DISTINCT order_id/state pairs prevent double counting within a state
The 100+ threshold applies to the delivered-orders denominator
Late rate returned as a fraction between 0 and 1

S4::which seller state had the worst lat.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    o.order_id,
    s.seller_state,
    CAST(o.order_delivered_customer_date AS DATE) > CAST(o.order_estimated_delivery_date AS DATE) AS is_late
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
  WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
    AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-01-01'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01'
)
SELECT seller_state,
       SUM(CASE WHEN is_late THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::DOUBLE / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS late_rate
FROM base
GROUP BY seller_state
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
ORDER BY late_rate DESC
LIMIT 1;
S4::which seller state had the worst lat.explanation: Computes the 2017 late delivery rate (delivered-late / delivered with a delivery date) per seller state and returns the worst state among those with at least 100 delivered orders.
assumptions: 2017 filters on order_purchase_timestamp (Jan 1–Dec 31, 2017)
Seller state comes from the sellers table via order_items
Late rate = delivered orders with delivery date after estimated date / delivered orders with a non-null delivery date, per the business rule
An order with items from sellers in multiple states counts toward each such state
Only states with 100+ delivered orders (with a delivery date) in 2017 are considered

S1::how are orders from s\u00e3o paulo-b.sql:
SELECT AVG(r.review_score) AS avg_review_score
FROM reviews r
WHERE r.order_id IN (
    SELECT oi.order_id
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
    WHERE lower(s.seller_city) IN ('sao paulo', 'são paulo'
);
S1::how are orders from s\u00e3o paulo-b.explanation: Returns the average review score across all reviews of orders that include at least one item sold by a seller located in São Paulo.
assumptions: 'São Paulo-based' means the seller's city (seller_city = 'são paulo'), not the state of SP
An order qualifies if it has at least one order_item from a São Paulo seller
All order statuses are included since no status was specified
Some orders have multiple reviews; all review rows are averaged

S4::how are orders from s\u00e3o paulo-b.sql:

WHERE r.order_id IN (
    SELECT oi.order_id

    WHERE s.seller_state = 'SP'
